Definition: from the same as G2436; propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. prompt or willing:--cheerful.
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, hilarós means cheerful. It occurs just once, in 2 Corinthians.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple here: hilarós means cheerful, and I do not stretch it further.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
